analysis.investment_thesis: Greaves Cotton is a legacy industrial-to-EV pivot story that has destroyed shareholder value — operating margins collapsed from 13% (2016) to 3.9% (2025), with net losses in 4 of the last 5 years and chronically negative free cash flow. At ₹3,760 Cr market cap and 34.6x P/E, the stock is priced for a turnaround that hasn't materialized.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 55.8% — skin in the game, no stake dilution
Low Debt/Equity of 0.12 — balance sheet not overleveraged despite cash burn
Revenue recovering to ₹2,918 Cr (2025) with last-5-year expanding trend — legacy engine business still breathing
key_risks: Chronic cash destruction: Free cash flow negative every year 2022-2025 (cumulative FCF burn ~₹553 Cr), OCF positive only 1/5 years
EV pivot (Ampere, ELE brands) has obliterated margins — operating income fell from ₹272 Cr (2019) to ₹137 Cr (2025) on higher revenue
Valuation mismatch: P/E of 34.6x on a near-breakeven company (₹-6 Cr net profit in 2025) with ROE of just 4.1%
red_flags: Market cap ₹3,760 Cr — 4x outside Kedia SMILE sweet spot of <₹1,000 Cr
Net losses in 2021 (₹-19 Cr), 2022 (₹-35 Cr), 2024 (₹-367 Cr — likely EV subsidiary impairment) and near-zero in 2025
Finance costs compounding at 36% CAGR — rising debt dependency (borrowings ₹20 Cr → ₹185 Cr in 4 years)
Other Income swung to -₹270 Cr in 2024 — signals massive write-downs on EV investments, hidden balance sheet damage
Operating margin of 3.9% — no operational leverage visible despite revenue recovery; EBITDA CAGR -3.8% over 9 years
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Greaves Cotton is a textbook case of a legacy business that attempted a disruptive pivot without the unit economics to support it. Founded in 1859, the company built a solid engines/gensets franchise delivering ₹200+ Cr profits through 2019. But the aggressive move into electric two-wheelers (Ampere) and three-wheelers has been value-destructive — cumulative net losses since 2021 exceed ₹400 Cr, the 2024 write-down of ~₹270 Cr in Other Income signals the EV bets are being marked down, and free cash flow has been negative for four consecutive years burning through ₹553 Cr. Revenue growing at 6.8% CAGR while operating income shrinks at -4.3% CAGR is the opposite of the operational leverage Kedia looks for.

From a SMILE lens, this stock fails on nearly every dimension that matters. Size is wrong at ₹3,760 Cr — Kedia's multibagger hunting ground is ₹100-1,000 Cr where information asymmetry exists. Valuation is wrong at 34.6x P/E — Kedia demands 8-15x entry. The transformation story (ICE-to-EV) exists on paper but execution has been abysmal with no clear inflection visible. The only saving grace is promoter holding at 55.8% and a clean balance sheet (D/E 0.12), but neither compensates for the cash hemorrhage. Until EV subsidiaries turn FCF-positive and operating margins recover above 8-10%, this is a value trap dressed as a transformation story.
